## What's built
As of October 6, in the team repo. The build follows Natalie's Supabase schema; the data model below is the target it converges on.
| Part | Where | What it does |

| Import engine | `import-engine/` | Reads AAFE's Give Lively export, converts times to UTC, splits free-text guest lists, matches buyers and guests, builds the import report. Plain TypeScript, no screens, 94 tests |

| Database and server functions | `prototype/database/` | Natalie's schema and seed, plus the import tables (`import_runs`, `import_review`, `tier_mappings`). Every staff action goes through a function that writes the history |
| Server jobs | `prototype/supabase/functions/` | Give Lively sync (this gala's page only) and the email sender (staff-approved only) |
| Staff app | `prototype/staff-app/` | Natalie's staff workspace; real sign-in in review (PR #27); still on demo data |
| Sponsor portal | `prototype/guest-portal/` | Natalie's guest-name form on a private link; English, 中文, Español |
| Checks on every PR | `.github/workflows/` | Secret scan, import engine tests, backend tests (97, run on an in-memory Postgres) |

**Secrets are stored as hashes.** Sponsor links and QR e-tickets are random, shown only in the email that carries them, and stored only as hashes. A QR code belongs to one seat and stops working the morning after the gala, or as soon as the seat gets a different guest.

## Built and tested

The import works end to end in code: a file in AAFE's export format goes through the import engine and into the database in one step that either fully succeeds or changes nothing. What's left is the staff app's upload screen (frontend pair).
- **Import engine** (`import-engine/`): reads the file, converts times to UTC, splits guest lists, matches buyers and guests, builds the report. 94 automated tests.

- **Database side** (`prototype/database/backend.sql`): skips purchases it has seen, never overwrites a name a sponsor or staff entered, keeps a run record for every upload, and puts close calls in the review queue. 97 automated tests, including a sample file run all the way t…
Three choices settled while building (Oct 6; Natalie reviewing in Slack):
| Question | Decision |
| A guest list with clear names and one unclear entry | The clear names are pre-filled for the sponsor to confirm; the unclear one shows as written. More names than seats pre-fills nothing |
| The same guest name on two sponsors' orders | A possible duplicate for staff to confirm, unless the email or a known organization also matches |
| An upload before this gala's Give Lively page is set | The upload stops and lists the pages in the file; staff pick one, once a year |

changes.before: Updated Oct 5 for AAFE's real Give Lively export: one row per purchase, no transaction ID, and guest names typed into one free-text box. The full spec in the repo is being revised to match.
changes.after: Updated Oct 5 for AAFE's real Give Lively export: one row per purchase, no transaction ID, and guest names typed into one free-text box. Updated Oct 6 with Natalie's second review: a tier mapping staff fill in once per gala, and a filter on the gala's Give Lively page name.

changes.after: Identify | Each row is one purchase. With no transaction ID, a purchase is recognized by the buyer's email and purchase time (in UTC), so re-importing never duplicates it, even if the tier is renamed.

## Tier names and the gala page

- **Tier mapping.** AAFE's export says just "Ticket" for the tier, which matches no package. Staff link each Give Lively tier name to a package once per gala; every later upload uses it. A name with no link goes to review, and linking it there saves it.
- **Gala page.** Each gala stores its Give Lively page name ("AAFE's 52nd Annual Gala"). Only that page's purchases are imported; rows from another page are skipped and listed in the report.

changes.after: - **Per-ticket ID:** none, and no transaction ID either. A purchase is keyed on email + purchase time in UTC.
- **Tier:** just "Ticket" in the sample, so staff map tier names to packages (Oct 6).
- **Page name:** "AAFE's 52nd Annual Gala", so the import filters on each gala's page name, not a fixed "AAFE Gala 2027" setting (Oct 6).
